props.title: Heights

sections.content: Heights (2005) represents a masterful ensemble drama in the vein of Short Cuts (1993) and Magnolia (1999), weaving together multiple storylines across a single day in New York City. Director Chris Terrio crafts an intimate portrait of interconnected lives, anchored by Glenn Close's powerful performance as Diana, a renowned stage actress whose personal and professional lives begin to unravel. The film's exploration of sexuality, infidelity, and artistic ambition echoes similar themes found in The Hours (2002) and Closer (2004), but with a distinctly New York theater world backdrop.

sections.content: The film's theatrical elements draw fascinating parallels to other stage-to-screen crossovers like Birdman (2014) and All About Eve (1950). Elizabeth Banks delivers a breakthrough dramatic performance as Isabel, a photographer whose engagement begins to crack under the weight of secrets. The film's sophisticated handling of LGBTQ+ themes was notably progressive for 2005, predating similar nuanced treatments in films like A Single Man (2009) and Carol (2015).

Cinematographer Jim Denault's elegant lensing of Manhattan creates a sophisticated urban landscape that becomes its own character, reminiscent of Gordon Willis's work in Manhattan (1979). The vertical nature of the city - its towering buildings and social hierarchies - gives the film its namesake and metaphorical framework, examining how characters at different "heights" of success and society interact and influence each other's lives. sections.content: The film's insider view of New York's theater scene provides rich dramatic territory, particularly through Glenn Close's Diana, who channels the competitive, ambitious spirit of the stage world. This portrayal stands alongside other notable theatrical dramas like Opening Night (1977) and All That Jazz (1979), examining the personal costs of artistic pursuit. The integration of Shakespeare's "Macbeth" into the narrative adds layers of meaning about ambition and betrayal that resonate throughout the interconnected stories.
